chunks: From him, from al-Hus-Husayn, from an-Nadr, from ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"Whoever wakes up intending to fast, then decides to break the fast, he may break it from the time of his decision until midday; then he must make up that day. If he decides to fast after the sun has risen, let him fast, for it will be counted for him from the hour in which he made the intention."

key_terms.بَدَا لَهُ: It appeared to him / He decided

ai.seo_question: Can I break my fast after dawn and still have a valid fast if I decide to continue?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility in breaking a fast after dawn, specifying that the window to invalidate it closes at midday (Zawal), after which the fast is considered complete from the moment of renewed intention. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that intention (niyyah) can be made during the day for obligatory fasts, distinguishing it from the Hanafi view of fixed intention at night, and underscores the importance of the sun's zenith as the critical temporal marker for fast validity.
